initial_presentation: Case 2 involves a 34-year-old female of Greek descent. She experienced repeated pathological fractures starting at age 28. From age 30, she exhibited increasing cognitive and behavioral symptoms resembling frontotemporal changes.

A 28-year-old male underwent simultaneous bilateral SMILE for myopia correction at a private clinic and presented to our clinic 2 days later with visual loss and severe ocular pain in his right eye. His medical history showed he was immunocompetent before surgery, with no history of HSV keratitis and no apparent infection risk factors. He did not use contact lenses. Upon presentation, his uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA) was reduced to counting fingers at 30 cm in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye.

A 35-year-old woman with no history of smoking experienced left back pain following a 2-hour flight and began coughing the next day. She has a medical history of acute myeloid leukemia (French-American-British classification type M1) diagnosed at 1 year and 8 months old. She underwent an allogenic bone marrow transplant from her older sister at 2 years and 3 months old. Methotrexate was used as a preventive measure. At 3 years old, she developed a rash and symptoms including dry mouth and reduced tear production.

A 50-year-old female patient visited the Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology Department for an evaluation of an ulceration on her upper lip, including the philtrum, which had been present for 2 years. The patient reported a history of chewing tobacco multiple times daily for approximately 10 years. Clinical examination showed a large, destructive ulceration with induration, measuring approximately 7 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm. This ulceration extended beyond the middle third of the upper lip area, involving the outer skin and exposing the upper anterior mucosa. No regional lymphadenopathy was observed.
A 19-year-old male, the eldest of four siblings, was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus type 1 at the age of 10. He presented with complaints of decreased vision.

A 4-year-old female patient presented with complaints of discolored teeth, pain in the lower jaw, and significant wear of all teeth. The patient's father reported that the discoloration had been present since the teeth first erupted. Family history indicated that the patient's mother, maternal grandfather, two aunts, and their sons also experienced similar dental issues. The mother and her sisters had not sought dental treatment, resulting in progressive tooth substance loss. There was no reported history of bone abnormalities in the family. Clinical examination showed extensive loss of enamel and dentin, with teeth exhibiting hard brown dentin and worn incisal and occlusal surfaces, in some cases down to the gingival level. The mandibular first molars were exposed, and an abscess was noted in relation to the mandibular right first molar.

A 51-year-old male presented with a 2-year history of snoring and changes in voice. He reported loud snoring and had been observed to experience obstructive sleep apnea along with excessive daytime sleepiness. His Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) score was 13. He did not report any episodes of shortness of breath. His medical history included mild hypertension and diabetes. The patient’s height was 160 cm, weight was 62 kg, and body mass index (BMI) was 24.2 kg/m2. Physical examination revealed a Friedman tongue position of grade III, where only the soft palate was visible, and the tonsils were not visible as they were hidden in the tonsillar fossa.

A 52-year-old woman presented with thickened skin on her palms and soles, a condition that started in her childhood. She also reported changes in one of her toes that began a few years ago. She is part of a family with five generations affected by similar symptoms. Her mother had a finger amputated due to the progression of the same condition. On physical examination, there was widespread thickening of the skin on the palms and soles, with constrictive bands observed on the fifth toe of the left foot. Additionally, there was generalized scaling of the skin, but no hearing loss was noted.

An 86-year-old female with no significant past medical history presented with a headache persisting for 1 year. The headache occurred exclusively at night, starting around 12 a.m., waking her up and lasting for 2–3 hours. She rated the headache severity between 4 and 7 on a scale of 1 to 10. The headache was unilateral, primarily around the right orbital region, occasionally involving the auricular area, and was described as a dull aching, non-pulsating pain without radiation. Sometimes, the headache was accompanied by right-sided rhinorrhea. There was no conjunctival injection, tearing, nausea, vomiting, or sensitivity to light or sound. She reported uninterrupted sleep before the onset of these headache episodes. There were no indications of obstructive sleep apnea or other sleep-related disorders. She had no history of migraines, recurrent headaches, seizures, neuralgias, or other neurological conditions. Family history was unremarkable. Despite multiple medical consultations, her symptoms persisted. On examination, she appeared well at rest with a regular heart rate of 70 beats/min, blood pressure of 142/68 mmHg, and clear lung fields.

Patient 2 is a 73-year-old Caucasian male. At the age of 72, the patient began experiencing widespread itching, which was soon followed by intense pain, stiffness, and swelling in his left foot. The pain and stiffness rapidly spread to both legs, accompanied by extremely painful muscle cramps, ultimately resulting in the patient becoming dependent on a wheelchair.
